claims: A perigee raise maneuver is an orbital maneuver where a spacecraft fires its engines at apogee to raise its perigee.
The NASA Artemis II mission requires a 100-mile (roughly 160-185 km) altitude orbit for its crewed Orion spacecraft.
The Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) performs a perigee raise burn approximately 49 minutes after launch for Artemis II.
The ICPS perigee raise burn brings the Orion capsule into a stable orbit.
The ICPS perigee raise burn reduces the risk of the Orion capsule re-entering the Earth's atmosphere too early.
To raise the perigee, a spacecraft must perform a prograde burn at apogee.
Increasing speed at apogee increases the altitude at the opposite side of the orbit.
For Artemis II, the ICPS performs an initial perigee raise to over 100 miles.
For Artemis II, the ICPS performs an additional burn after the initial raise to further optimize the orbit for future maneuvers
